newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian tolar strength hurting exporters - P.M.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian tolar strength hurting exporters - P.M.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Thursday the strength of the tolar was hurting the nation's export industry.
"I think the strength of the tolar is becoming a problem for our exporters," Drnovsek told Reuters in an interview.
The tolar was quoted at 90.2 to the mark on Thursday, compared with 88.0 at the start of the year.
Drnovsek noted that Slovenia's independent central bank had employed some instruments to bring the value of the tolar down.
"But these are only slight movements," he said.
The Bank of Slovenia has insisted it will not change its monetary policy despite complaints from exporters who say they are being squeezed.
